questions.stem: To separate a mixture of sand and common salt dissolved in water, one would use in sequence:
questions.explanation: Sand is insoluble, salt is soluble. Step 1 — filtration separates the sand (on the filter paper) from the salt solution (the filtrate). Step 2 — evaporation of the filtrate leaves behind salt crystals. Distillation would also work for step 2 if you wanted to recover the water as well.

questions.stem: Which separation technique would best suit separating iodine from common salt?
questions.explanation: Iodine sublimes (directly turns from solid to vapour on heating), salt does not. On gentle heating, iodine vapour can be collected and re-deposited; salt stays behind. Other sublimable solids — ammonium chloride, naphthalene, camphor, dry ice. Magnetic separation works for iron filings. Centrifugation — for suspensions (e.g., blood plasma from cells).

options.option_text: Two miscible liquids with different boiling points

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation — for miscible liquids with different boiling points: crude oil into petrol, diesel, kerosene; liquid air into N₂ and O₂; ethanol-water (azeotropic limit 95.6 %). A fractionating column helps repeated vaporisation-condensation cycles to improve separation. Two immiscible liquids (oil + water) are separated with a separating funnel.

questions.stem: Which technique is used to separate colour pigments in ink or the constituents of chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Chromatography — different components of a mixture travel at different speeds through a stationary phase carried by a moving solvent (mobile phase). Types — paper, thin-layer, column, gas-liquid, HPLC. Widely used for analysis in biology, chemistry, forensics, drug testing. Crystallisation — purifying a solid from solution by controlled cooling / evaporation.

questions.stem: Iron filings mixed with sulphur powder can be separated by using:
questions.explanation: Iron is ferromagnetic; sulphur is not. Running a magnet through the mixture picks up the iron filings and leaves sulphur behind. If the mixture is HEATED first, iron and sulphur combine to form iron(II) sulphide (FeS) — a chemical change — and the mixture can no longer be separated by a magnet. A classic demonstration of 'physical vs chemical change'.

questions.stem: To obtain pure water from sea water, the most suitable technique is:
questions.explanation: Sea water contains dissolved salts that filtration can't remove. Simple distillation boils water → collects pure condensate. Reverse osmosis (RO) — pushes water through a semi-permeable membrane that blocks salt ions. Large-scale desalination plants use RO (e.g., Minjur, Nemmeli in Chennai; big ones in the Gulf). Evaporation alone gives water vapour but without condensation you have no liquid pure water to collect. or reverse osmosis.

questions.stem: A centrifuge separates a mixture based on difference in:
questions.explanation: A centrifuge spins samples at high speed; denser components migrate to the outer edge (bottom of the tube), lighter components stay near the axis. Uses — separating blood plasma from cells, cream from milk, dust from industrial gases (cyclone separators), uranium isotope enrichment (gas centrifuges). Ultracentrifuges run at > 100,000 rpm for protein and DNA studies.
